s: a male given name from Middle High German, origin of the English Conrad
Konrad.et: From Middle High German Kuonrāt, from Old High German Kuonrad, Chuonrad, from Proto-West Germanic *Kōnirād; equivalent to Proto-West Germanic *kōnī (“bold, brave”) + *rād (“counsel”). The modern spelling with final -d has been influenced by unshifted Central G…

s: Konradsreuth (a municipality of Hof district, Upper Franconia, Bavaria, Germany)
Konradsreuth.et:
First attested as Conratsrute in 1266.
By surface analysis, Konrad + -s- + -reuth.
The suffix -reuth indicates a clearance settlement.
